scenarios: Kịch bản chính (~50%): chỉnh về 4.168–4.175 trong phiên Á hoặc quanh GDP Trung Quốc – MUA khi nến 45m/1H đóng xanh, TP 4.195 → 4.205.
Kịch bản phụ (~30%): đi thẳng lên 4.196–4.206 – không đuổi mua; nến 45m/1H đỏ thì BÁN lướt nhỏ; nến 1H đóng trên 4.212 thì bỏ bán, chờ hồi 4.200–4.205 để MUA hướng 4.221 → 4.243.
Kịch bản xấu (~20%): nến 1H đóng dưới 4.155 – đứng ngoài; mốc tiếp theo 4.142 rồi 4.120.
Rủi ro: hôm nay không có tin đỏ USD. 09:00 GDP quý 3 Trung Quốc (dự báo 4,4%); 21:00 NAHB (tin nhẹ). Tin Hormuz/Iran có thể làm giá giật 10–15 giá bất cứ lúc nào.
scenarios_en: The plan: buy 4,168–4,175 (stop 4,153 · TP1 4,195 → TP2 4,205) · sell 4,196–4,206 (stop 4,218 · TP1 4,186 → TP2 4,174). Only on a confirming 45m/1H close.
Base case (~50%): a dip into 4,168–4,175 during Asia or around China's GDP – buy a green 45m/1H close, targets 4,195 → 4,205.
Alternative (~30%): a straight run into 4,196–4,206 – don't chase; a red 45m/1H close is a small short; a 1H close above 4,212 kills the short and I buy the 4,200–4,205 retest toward 4,221 → 4,243.
Bear case (~20%): a 1H close under 4,155 – step aside; 4,142, then 4,120.
Risk: no high-impact U.S. data today. China Q3 GDP at 10:00 PM ET (est. 4.4%); NAHB at 10:00 AM ET (minor). Hormuz/Iran headlines can whip gold $10–$15 at any time.

market_picture.text: Cuối tuần chiến sự nóng hơn – thủy lôi ở Hormuz, Iran dọa «kế hoạch tác chiến mới», Ukraine đánh kho dầu St. Petersburg – nhưng thị trường mở cửa bình tĩnh: Brent lùi 1,4% về 108,4, chứng khoán tương lai bật lại (Nasdaq +0,8%) vì nhà đầu tư bắt đáy nhóm AI. Thứ thực sự đỡ vàng là lợi suất: 10 năm lùi về 5,065%, lợi suất thực chốt tuần ở 2,74%, Fed im lặng tới 29/10 với 83,9% cửa giữ lãi tháng 10 – trong khi USD đứng yên (DXY 101,85). Vì vậy vàng mở cửa tuần +20 giá, từ 4.164,6 lên 4.184,6: chi phí giữ vàng rẻ đi chứ không phải hoảng loạn. Quan điểm của tôi: phiên Á nghiêng tăng, nhưng 4.196–4.206 là trần đã chặn giá bốn lần trong hai tuần (9, 12, 13 và 16/10). Mốc quyết định là 4.212 (nến 1H đóng trên thì trần thành sàn) và 4.155 (thủng là tôi sai). Việc cần làm: không đuổi 4.184, chờ chỉnh 4.168–4.175 để MUA; chạm trần mà có nến đỏ thì BÁN lướt nhỏ.

market_picture_en.text: The weekend added war risk – mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran warning of a 'new operational plan,' Ukraine hitting a St. Petersburg oil terminal – yet the open is calm: Brent is down 1.4% at $108.40 and stock futures are bouncing (Nasdaq +0.8%) as dip buyers return to AI names. What's really carrying gold is yields: the 10-year is back to 5.065%, 10-year real yields ended the week at 2.74%, and the Fed is in blackout until Oct 29 with 83.9% odds of an October hold – while the dollar goes nowhere (DXY 101.85). That's why gold opened the week up $20, from 4,164.60 to 4,184.60: a cheaper cost of carry, not panic. My view: the Asia session leans bullish, but 4,196–4,206 has capped gold four times in two weeks (Oct 9, 12, 13 and 16). The levels that matter are 4,212 (a 1H close above turns the ceiling into a floor) and 4,155 (lose it and I'm wrong). The job: don't chase 4,184 – buy a dip into 4,168–4,175, and scalp a red close at the ceiling.

sections.h: Kết quả kế hoạch thứ Sáu
sections.p: Lệnh MUA 19:15 đi trọn: TP1 4.185 lúc 20:50, phần còn lại chạm TP2 4.198 lúc 21:25 (đỉnh 4.198,2 – vừa đủ, sát nút). Kế hoạch 21:07 thì khác: giá không lên tới vùng BÁN 4.200–4.210 (thiếu 1,8 giá) rồi bị bán chốt lời cuối tuần, xuyên thẳng vùng MUA 4.168–4.176 lúc 22:25 xuống 4.155,8 (01:50 sáng thứ Bảy). Không có nến 45m hay 1H nào đóng xanh trong vùng, nên theo đúng luật tôi không vào – và tránh được nhịp âm ~16 giá. Sáng nay, nến 1H đầu tuần (05:00–06:00) đóng xanh 4.173,5 ngay trong vùng: đó mới là tín hiệu MUA, hiện lời ~9 giá. Bài học tôi rút ra: giá ba lần khựng ngay dưới 4.200 (4.198,2; 4.199; 4.197) – đặt TP trước mốc tròn vài giá, đừng đặt đúng vào nó.

sections.h: Mở cửa tuần: vì sao vàng nhích lên
sections.p: Cuối tuần chiến sự nóng hơn – thủy lôi ở Hormuz, Iran dọa «kế hoạch tác chiến mới», Ukraine đánh kho dầu St. Petersburg – nhưng thị trường mở cửa khá bình tĩnh: Brent còn lùi 1,4%, chứng khoán tương lai bật lại vì nhà đầu tư bắt đáy nhóm AI. Thứ đẩy vàng là lợi suất: 10 năm lùi về 5,065%, trong khi USD đứng yên (DXY 101,85). Fed đang im lặng tới 29/10 và thị trường đặt 83,9% cửa giữ lãi tháng 10, nên không có ai «nói» làm lợi suất bật lại trong tuần này. Vàng +20 giá không phải vì hoảng loạn, mà vì chi phí giữ vàng rẻ đi.

sections.h: Tôi giao dịch phiên Á thế nào
sections.p: Tôi giữ lệnh MUA kích hoạt lúc 06:00 nhưng hạ TP1 về 4.195 – chạm là chốt 60% và dời SL về điểm vào. Không đuổi giá 4.182–4.184. Ai chưa có lệnh thì chờ chỉnh về 4.168–4.175 và nến 45m/1H đóng xanh. Vùng 4.196–4.206 là trần đã chặn giá suốt hai tuần: chạm trần mà nến 45m/1H đóng đỏ thì tôi BÁN lướt nhỏ, còn nếu nến 1H đóng trên 4.212 thì tôi bỏ ý định bán và mua lại khi giá hồi về 4.200. 09:00 có GDP Trung Quốc – tôi không mở lệnh mới trước khi nến 45m/1H sau tin đóng cửa.

sections.p: The 8:15 AM ET long ran its course: TP1 4,185 at 9:50 AM ET, and the runner tagged TP2 4,198 at 10:25 AM ET (high 4,198.20 – by a hair). The 10:07 AM ET plan was a different story. Gold never reached the 4,200–4,210 short (missed by $1.80), then got sold into the weekend, slicing through the 4,168–4,176 buy zone at 11:25 AM ET down to 4,155.80 at 2:50 PM ET. No 45m or 1H candle closed green inside the zone, so by the rules I stayed out – and skipped a roughly $16 drawdown. The real signal came at tonight's open: the 6–7 PM ET hourly candle closed green at 4,173.50 inside the zone. That long is up about $9. Lesson: gold has stalled just under 4,200 three times (4,198.20, 4,199, 4,197). Set targets a few dollars in front of the round number, not on it.

sections.h: The Sunday open: why gold is bid
sections.p: The weekend added more war risk – mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran warning of a 'new operational plan,' Ukraine hitting a St. Petersburg oil terminal – yet the open was calm. Brent is actually down 1.4%, and stock futures are bouncing as dip buyers step back into AI names. What's lifting gold is yields: the 10-year is back to 5.065% while the dollar is flat (DXY 101.85). The Fed is in its blackout until Oct 29 with 83.9% odds of an October hold, so nobody is on the wire to talk yields back up this week. Gold's $20 pop isn't panic – it's a cheaper cost of carry.

sections.h: How I'm trading the Asia session
sections.p: I'm holding the long that triggered at the 7:00 PM ET hourly close, but I've trimmed TP1 to 4,195 – hit it, bank 60% and move the stop to breakeven. I'm not chasing 4,182–4,184. If you're flat, wait for a dip into 4,168–4,175 and a green 45m/1H close. 4,196–4,206 has capped gold for two weeks: a red 45m/1H close up there is a small short; a 1H close above 4,212 kills the short idea and I'd buy the 4,200 retest instead. China Q3 GDP hits at 10:00 PM ET – no new entries until the first 45m/1H candle after the release has closed.

sections.h: How the 8:15 AM ET plan played out

sections.h: Why gold is where it is
sections.p: This morning's prints ran hot versus forecasts but none were high-impact – the market already digested this week's CPI/PPI. The real drive is the dollar and yields: DXY 101.65 (−0.40%, day low 101.58) on track for a weekly loss; the 10-year eased to 5.081% (day high 5.133%) after Warsh gave no October hike signal – Kitco has October hike odds near 15% and December near 89%. S&P futures −0.1%, VIX 16.1 – no panic. Brent $105.40 with Hormuz still tense (Kitco) keeps a geopolitical bid under gold. My read: the 4,155 flush was a stop-run inside an uptrend, not a reversal; buyers just proved it with that green 45m after the cash open.

sections.p: Đây là cuộc kéo co giữa USD và lợi suất. sections.p: None of today's four setups filled: the 4,158–4,165 buy (2:45 AM ET), 4,150–4,160 (4:45 AM ET), 4,160–4,167 (4:47 AM ET) and 4,155–4,165 (6:47 AM ET) – the deepest dip was 4,171.40 at 8:00 AM ET. The 4,198–4,212 sell zones never traded either; the day high stopped at 4,191.30 (5:15 AM ET). No win, no loss. I had the direction right – gold went up – but I set the buy zones too deep. The lesson: when the 45m through 4H all sit in the upper half of BB90, pullbacks tend to stop at the 38.2–50% retracement, rarely at 78.6%. So this morning's buy zone moves up to the 50–61.8% cluster.

sections.h: From the 6:47 AM ET note into the New York open
sections.p: Gold was near 4,178 at 6:47 AM ET. It bounced to 4,181.30 at 7:15 AM ET and then got sold steadily. The 7:15–8:00 AM ET 45-minute candle closed red at 4,171.60, the lowest since late Asia. The 4,171.40 low at 8:00 AM ET sits right above the 50% retracement (4,169.50) of the 4,147.80 → 4,191.30 leg, and gold has bounced to 4,176–4,177 at 8:25 AM ET (CNBC 4,176.20; gold-api.com 4,177.60). Anyone who chased 4,185–4,191 in London is underwater, and their stops sit around 4,170 – exactly the kind of pocket this market likes to sweep before the next leg.

sections.h: Why gold is where it is
sections.p: It's a tug-of-war between the dollar and yields. The dollar is soft: DXY 101.72 (−0.28% from the New York close), a day low of 101.58, and on track for its first weekly loss after three weekly gains (Reuters) – that's what lifted gold to 4,191. But the 10-year Treasury yield has bounced back to 5.102% (day high 5.123%) with the 2-year at 4.746%, and that's the brake that stopped gold from holding the high. On the Fed, Warsh gave nothing away and CME FedWatch shows an 87% chance of a hold in October (CNBC); the blackout starts Saturday ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC. Brent sits near $105.90 with Iran saying it's stepping up strikes around Hormuz (CNBC), which keeps a geopolitical bid under gold. S&P futures are up 0.2% and the VIX is 16.0 – no panic, so no rush into havens. My read: the drop from 4,191 is a technical pullback inside an uptrend, not a reversal.

Calendar (ForexFactory, ET): no high-impact U.S. data today. 8:30 AM import prices (est. +0.9%, prior 0.7%); 9:15 AM industrial production (est. +0.4%, prior 0.0%) and capacity utilization (est. 76.5%, prior 76.3%); 9:30 AM cash open; 2:00 PM federal budget balance (est. −$34.7B, prior −$166.8B); 4:00 PM TIC flows; 5:00 PM weekly close. Base case (~60%): gold dips into 4,162–4,169, runs the stops of the London chasers and turns higher – buy on a green 45m/1H close in the zone, targeting 4,185 and then 4,198 (R1, Oct 13 high). Alternative (~25%): no dip, and gold takes out 4,191 after the cash open – don't chase it; watch 4,200–4,210: a red 45m/1H close there is a small-size short, but a 1H close above 4,210 kills the short and I'll look to buy a retest of 4,198–4,203 toward 4,226 (R2). Bear case (~15%): a 1H close under 4,153 (1H BB90 mid) – step aside; next stops 4,147 and 4,121 (S1). Weekly marker: last Friday's close was about 4,193.80 – a weekly close above it turns the week green.

Big picture (primary trend up): the 45m, 1H, 2H, 3H and 4H all trade in the upper half of BB90 (mids 4,147 / 4,154 / 4,153 / 4,154 / 4,156); MACD is positive on the 2H/3H/4H with histograms at +2.9 / +5.0 / +5.1. Short term (the pullback): the 5m is below its mid at 4,179 with MA34 (4,177.90) under MA89 (4,179.50) and RSI 47; the 15m is below MA34 at 4,179 but above its MA89/mid at 4,167 with a negative MACD; the 30m holds above MA34 at 4,172 and MA89 at 4,148.50. The 45m/1H MACD just crossed down slightly (histograms −1.0 / −0.8) with RSI 54 / 57 – momentum is resting, not broken. Under the H79 rule (mirrored for an uptrend), a 5m/15m down-channel is just a pullback that tends to stall at the cluster of the 45m MA34 4,165.60 · 4H MA34 4,165.10 · 15m mid/MA89 4,167 · 50–61.8% Fib 4,169.50/4,164.40 – hence the 4,162–4,169 buy zone. The 4,200–4,210 sell zone lines up with the upper BB90 on the 45m (4,202), 3H (4,208.50), 1H (4,209) and 4H (4,209), plus R1 4,198 and the Oct 13 high of 4,197. Daily pivots from the Oct 15 session (high 4,176.90 · low 4,099.90 · close 4,170.20): P 4,149 · R1 4,198 · R2 4,226 · S1 4,121. My stance: buyers are still in control; I wait for price to come to my level, and I'm fine missing the trade if it doesn't.

sections.p: PPI tháng 9 ra lúc 19:30 nóng hơn hẳn dự báo: +1,3% so với tháng trước (dự báo 0,6%), PPI lõi +0,7%, so với cùng kỳ +6,3% – mạnh nhất từ 2022; bán lẻ +0,8% (dự báo 0,3%). Vàng bị bán xuống 4.138,1 lúc 19:35 khi DXY vọt lên 102,26 (19:40). Nhưng cú rơi không kéo dài: lợi suất 10 năm Mỹ quay đầu xuống 5,037% lúc 21:00, cổ phiếu AI bị bán mạnh (Nvidia −1,84%, Dell −6,8%), và cuối phiên, từ 02:00 đến 03:00, vàng bật một mạch từ 4.157 lên 4.176,9. Phiên Mỹ khép lại ở 4.170,1 (04:55). Ai bán khống đuổi theo tin PPI dưới 4.140 đêm qua đã bị kẹp.

Mở 05:00 ở 4.170,2, giá trôi dần xuống đáy Á 4.147,8 lúc 08:35 khi DXY nhích lên 102,09 và lợi suất 10 năm lên 5,096%. Từ 09:20 lực mua quay lại: chỉ 35 phút vàng đi từ 4.153 lên 4.178,3 (09:55). Chủ tịch Fed Warsh phát biểu lúc 10:30, giá rung về 4.163,5 (10:40) rồi bật ngay khi ông không đưa tín hiệu mới – "tôi không đoán trước các cuộc họp". Đỉnh Á 4.184,1 lúc 11:05, cùng lúc DXY chạm đáy 101,82. Phiên Á đóng 4.176,5 (13:55): cao 4.184,1 – thấp 4.147,8, biên độ ~36 giá.

Mở 14:00 ở 4.176,7, vàng lên 4.188,8 lúc 14:30 rồi đỉnh ngày 4.191,3 lúc 16:15. Đó cũng là chỗ hụt hơi: lợi suất 10 năm bật từ 5,073% lên 5,102% (15:15) và giữ ở đó, giá trượt về 4.175,2 lúc 17:05 – đúng Fib 38,2% của sóng 4.147,8 → 4.191,3 – rồi hồi lên 4.184. Lúc 17:50 giá quanh 4.178 (CNBC 4.177,9; gold-api.com 4.178,9), tăng ~8 giá so với giá đóng phiên Mỹ. sections.h: Vì sao giá tăng rồi hụt hơi
sections.p: Thứ nhất, USD yếu: DXY từ 102,26 đêm qua xuống 101,61 (−0,41% trong ngày), hướng tới tuần giảm đầu tiên sau 5 tuần; bảng Anh lên cao nhất hơn 3 tuần sau số liệu kinh tế Anh tốt (CNBC). Đây là lực đẩy vàng lên 4.191. Thứ hai, Fed: Warsh không hé bài, thị trường giữ ~87% khả năng Fed đứng yên tháng 10 nhưng ~91% tăng lãi tháng 12 (CME FedWatch, theo CNBC) – lãi cao lâu hơn vẫn là áp lực dài hạn. Thứ ba, lợi suất: 10 năm 5,102%, 2 năm 4,751% – vẫn rất cao sau CPI 3,7% và PPI 6,3%; đây là cái phanh khiến vàng không vượt nổi 4.191 dù USD giảm. Thứ tư, dầu và chiến sự: Brent ~105,9 USD, dòng tàu qua Hormuz mới ~68% bình thường (Reuters); Trump nói Iran xin dừng tấn công và hai bên đang đàm phán, nhưng vẫn để ngỏ đánh thêm (Middle East Eye) – dầu cao giữ lo ngại lạm phát. Thứ năm, tâm lý: cổ phiếu AI mất hơn 1.000 tỷ USD trong tuần, CDS 5 năm của CoreWeave có lúc vượt 1.140 điểm (CNBC), nhưng hôm nay chứng khoán châu Âu tăng (STOXX 600 +0,7%), VIX 16,1 – không có hoảng loạn để vàng bứt phá. Về dài hạn ANZ vẫn lạc quan: lợi suất và USD hạ nhiệt sẽ mở đường cho vàng vượt 5.000 USD năm 2027 (CNBC).

Thứ Sáu không có tin đỏ Mỹ nào trên ForexFactory: 19:30 giá nhập khẩu (dự báo +0,9%, kỳ trước 0,7%), 20:15 sản xuất công nghiệp (+0,4%, trước 0,0%) và công suất sử dụng (76,5%) – đều là tin tác động thấp; 01:00 sáng mai có cán cân ngân sách liên bang. Fed bước vào giai đoạn im lặng từ 17/10 trước cuộc họp 27–28/10, nên tối nay giá sẽ chạy theo lợi suất, USD, tin Iran/Hormuz và dòng chốt lời cuối tuần. Mốc cần nhớ: giá đóng tuần trước ~4.193,8 – đóng tuần trên mức này thì tuần này tăng; dưới đó là tuần giảm nhẹ (CNBC: −0,2% trong tuần lúc 4.184).

Giá 4.178 nằm trên MA34 45m (4.164,6), MA89 (4.147,0) và BB90 giữa (4.147,4); dải trên 4.203,4, dải dưới 4.091,5. MACD 45m còn dương (8,1/7,9) nhưng histogram co từ +1,5 (15:15) về +0,2, RSI14 56 – đà tăng chững lại. Khung lớn: 1H/2H/3H/4H đều ở nửa trên BB90 (giữa 4.154,3 / 4.153,1 / 4.154,5 / 4.156,2; MA89 4.153–4.156), MACD 4H đã cắt lên, histogram +5,8 → xu hướng chính tăng. Bộ lọc H79: 5m đã xuống dưới BB giữa (4.179,2), RSI 41; 15m MACD âm, giá sát MA34 4.178,4 → đây là nhịp chỉnh trong xu hướng tăng, thường dừng ở cụm MA34 45m / MA89 15m / Fib 61,8% 4.164–4.166, sâu hơn là cụm BB giữa – MA89 khung lớn 4.153–4.156. Pivot ngày (phiên 15/10: cao 4.176,9 · thấp 4.099,9 · đóng 4.170,1): P 4.149 · R1 4.198 · R2 4.226 · S1 4.121. Đỉnh/đáy: đỉnh tuần 4.199,2 (12/10), đỉnh ngày 4.191,3, đáy Á 4.147,8, đáy tuần 4.074,1 (14/10). Fib sóng 4.147,8 → 4.191,3: 38,2% 4.174,7 (đã giữ lúc 17:05), 50% 4.169,5, 61,8% 4.164,4, 78,6% 4.157,1. Vùng BÁN 4.200–4.210 trùng R1 4.198, đỉnh tuần 4.199 và BB90 trên 45m/1H/4H 4.203–4.209 – chỉ để lướt ngắn. Tôi đợi giá về vùng MUA, có nến 45m/1H đóng xanh mới vào, và chấp nhận lỡ lệnh nếu giá không về.

sections.p: Thursday's September PPI hit at 8:30 AM ET and ran far hotter than expected: +1.3% m/m (est. 0.6%), core +0.7%, and +6.3% y/y – the biggest gain since 2022 – with retail sales up 0.8% (est. 0.3%). Gold got knocked down to 4,138.10 at 8:35 AM ET as the DXY spiked to 102.26 (8:40 AM ET). The flush didn't last: the 10-year yield rolled over to 5.037% by 10:00 AM ET, AI names took a beating (Nvidia −1.84%, Dell −6.8%), and between 3:00 and 4:00 PM ET gold ripped from 4,157 to 4,176.90. It finished the New York day at 4,170.10 (5:55 PM ET). Anyone who chased the PPI short under 4,140 got squeezed.

Gold opened the overnight session at 4,170.20 at 6:00 PM ET and drifted to the Asian low of 4,147.80 at 9:35 PM ET as the DXY firmed to 102.09 and the 10-year climbed to 5.096%. Buyers came back at 10:20 PM ET: in 35 minutes gold ran from 4,153 to 4,178.30 (10:55 PM ET). Fed Chair Kevin Warsh took the stage at 11:30 PM ET; gold wobbled to 4,163.50 (11:40 PM ET) and bounced right back once it was clear he had nothing new – "I don't prejudge meetings." The Asian high of 4,184.10 came at 12:05 AM ET, right as the DXY bottomed at 101.82. Asia closed at 4,176.50 (2:55 AM ET): high 4,184.10, low 4,147.80, a ~$36 range.

London opened at 4,176.70 at 3:00 AM ET. Gold tagged 4,188.80 at 3:30 AM ET and then a day high of 4,191.30 at 5:15 AM ET. That's where it ran out of gas: the 10-year jumped from 5.073% to 5.102% (4:15 AM ET) and stayed there, and gold slipped to 4,175.20 at 6:05 AM ET – right on the 38.2% retracement of the 4,147.80 → 4,191.30 leg – before bouncing to 4,184. At 6:50 AM ET spot sits near 4,178 (CNBC 4,177.90; gold-api.com 4,178.90), up about $8 from the New York close. The tell: the DXY slid further to 101.58 (6:40 AM ET) and gold didn't follow – yields are in the driver's seat. Neither of this morning's buy setups (4,150–4,160 and 4,160–4,167) filled, and the 4,203–4,212 short never triggered; the dip stopped at 4,175.20. I'd rather miss a move than chase one.

sections.h: Why gold rose – and why it stalled
sections.p: First, a softer dollar: the DXY fell from 102.26 overnight to 101.61 (−0.41% on the day) and is headed for its first weekly loss in five; sterling hit a three-week high on solid UK data (CNBC). That's what lifted gold to 4,191. Second, the Fed: Warsh kept his cards close, so markets still price ~87% odds of an October hold but ~91% odds of a December hike (CME FedWatch via CNBC) – higher-for-longer remains the long-run headwind. Third, yields: the 10-year at 5.102% and the 2-year at 4.751% are still elevated after 3.7% CPI and 6.3% PPI; that's the brake that kept gold under 4,191 even as the dollar fell. Fourth, oil and the war: Brent is near $105.90 with Strait of Hormuz traffic only ~68% of normal (Reuters); President Trump says Iran asked for a halt to strikes and talks are under way, but he hasn't ruled out more (Middle East Eye) – expensive oil keeps inflation fears alive. Fifth, sentiment: the 20 biggest AI and chip stocks have shed more than $1 trillion this week and CoreWeave's five-year CDS briefly topped 1,140 bps (CNBC), yet European stocks are up today (STOXX 600 +0.7%) and the VIX is 16.1 – no panic bid to force a breakout. Longer term, ANZ says a retreat in yields and the dollar would pave the way for gold above $5,000 in 2027 (CNBC).

There's no high-impact U.S. data on Friday's ForexFactory calendar: 8:30 AM ET import prices (est. +0.9%, prior 0.7%), 9:15 AM ET industrial production (+0.4%, prior 0.0%) and capacity utilization (76.5%) – all low impact – plus the federal budget balance at 2:00 PM ET. The Fed enters its blackout period Saturday ahead of the Oct. 27–28 meeting, so today's tape will trade off yields, the dollar, Iran/Hormuz headlines and Friday profit-taking. Level to watch for the weekly close: last Friday's ~4,193.80 – settle above it and the week is green; below it, a small weekly loss (CNBC had gold −0.2% on the week at 4,184).

At 4,178, gold is above the 45m MA34 (4,164.60), MA89 (4,147.00) and BB90 mid (4,147.40); upper band 4,203.40, lower band 4,091.50. The 45m MACD is still positive (8.1/7.9) but the histogram has shrunk from +1.5 (4:15 AM ET) to +0.2, and RSI(14) is 56 – momentum is flattening. Higher timeframes: the 1H/2H/3H/4H all trade in the upper half of BB90 (mids 4,154.30 / 4,153.10 / 4,154.50 / 4,156.20; MA89 4,153–4,156), and the 4H MACD has crossed up with a +5.8 histogram → the primary trend is up. H79 filter: the 5m has slipped under its mid (4,179.20) with RSI at 41, and the 15m MACD has turned negative with price sitting on its MA34 (4,178.40) → this is a pullback inside an uptrend, which typically finds buyers at the 45m MA34 / 15m MA89 / 61.8% Fib cluster at 4,164–4,166, or deeper at the higher-timeframe mid/MA89 cluster at 4,153–4,156. Daily pivots (Thursday's session: high 4,176.90 · low 4,099.90 · close 4,170.10): P 4,149 · R1 4,198 · R2 4,226 · S1 4,121. Key highs/lows: week high 4,199.20 (Monday), day high 4,191.30, Asian low 4,147.80, week low 4,074.10 (Wednesday). Fibonacci of the 4,147.80 → 4,191.30 leg: 38.2% 4,174.70 (held at 6:05 AM ET), 50% 4,169.50, 61.8% 4,164.40, 78.6% 4,157.10. The 4,200–4,210 sell zone lines up R1 4,198, the 4,199 week high and the 45m/1H/4H upper bands at 4,203–4,209 – scalp territory only. My read: bulls still own this tape, but anyone buying 4,185–4,191 right now is standing in the wrong spot, with stops sitting just under 4,175. I'm waiting for price to come to me, entering only on a green 45m/1H close in the zone – and if it never comes, I'm fine missing it.

market_picture_en.text: Gold is caught between two forces today, and yields are winning. A softer dollar – the DXY down to 101.58, a session low and headed for its first weekly loss in five (CNBC) – pushed gold to 4,191. But the 10-year bounced back to 5.10% after a week of hot inflation data (September PPI +6.3% y/y), and FedWatch still prices ~91% odds of a December hike (CNBC) – so the dollar kept falling and gold didn't follow. Warsh gave nothing away and the Fed goes quiet Saturday; Iran/Hormuz risk (Brent near $105.90, Reuters) and the AI-stock rout (CNBC) keep a haven floor under the metal. My view: the primary trend is still up, but as long as the 10-year holds above 5.1%, gold needs to pull back into 4,155–4,165 to reload; only a 4H close above 4,200 opens 4,226 and then 4,300. The play: don't chase 4,185–4,191 – buy the dip.

sections.p: Spot gold was ~4,178 at 2:45 AM ET, dipped only to 4,176.50 (2:55 AM ET) and then ran to a fresh day high of 4,188.80 at 3:30 AM ET as Europe opened. A bounce in Treasury yields pulled it back to 4,178.10 (4:15 AM ET), and it was holding 4,183–4,185 at 4:47 AM ET. A tight ~12-point range over two hours.

The dollar slid to 101.73 on the DXY (3:35 AM ET) as European stocks opened higher, lifting gold to the day high. The 10-year then climbed from 5.073% to 5.102% (4:15 AM ET), capping bullion under 4,190. No high-impact data in the window.

Right on direction: the up-channel held above 4,170 and price cleared R1 at 4,184 as expected. But there was no dip into the 4,158–4,165 buy zone (low 4,176.50) and no rally into the 4,198–4,208 sell zone (high 4,188.80) – nothing filled, no new TP or stop hits. Earlier closed calls stand in the log: Thursday's London short +21 points, the 6:47 AM ET short +12, the Asian short +21, the New York short −8.

strategies.trend_en: H79 filter (spot 4,183.40 at 3:45 AM ET bar): 45m/1H/2H/3H/4H all trade in the upper half of BB90 (mids 4,147.50 / 4,154 / 4,153 / 4,154.50 / 4,156) → primary uptrend. On the 5m/15m/30m/45m price is above MA34 and MA34 above MA89 (15m 4,171.80 / 4,162.80; 45m 4,162 / 4,147). 3H/4H MACD has crossed up; 1H RSI 62. Upper bands: 45m 4,203.50 · 1H 4,208 · 3H/4H 4,209 · 2H 4,214.60.
entryZones: Mua 4.160 – 4.167 (BB giữa/MA89 15m 4.163 · MA34 45m 4.162 · MA34 30m 4.167 · Fib 61,8% sóng 4.147,8→4.188,8 = 4.163,5). Vào khi giá chỉnh về vùng và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng xanh xác nhận; không dùng nến 15m/30m. Dừng lỗ 4.147 (dưới đáy 4.147,8 sáng nay và BB giữa 45m 4.147,5). TP1 4.188 (đỉnh ngày) – chốt 50–70%, dời SL về điểm vào; TP2 4.200, phần còn lại để 4.217. Nến 1H đóng dưới 4.153 (BB giữa 1H) thì bỏ lệnh mua.
entryZones_en: Buy 4,160–4,167 (15m mid/MA89 4,163 · 45m MA34 4,162 · 30m MA34 4,167 · 61.8% Fib of the 4,147.80→4,188.80 leg = 4,163.50). Enter on a dip into the zone with a green 45m or 1H close; never on a 15m/30m close. Stop 4,147 (under this morning's 4,147.80 low and the 45m mid at 4,147.50). TP1 4,188 (day high) – take 50–70% and move the stop to breakeven; TP2 4,200, runner toward 4,217. A 1H close under 4,153 (1H mid) cancels the long.
sellZones: Bán 4.203 – 4.212 (BB90 trên 45m 4.203,5 · 1H 4.208 · 3H/4H 4.209 · ngay trên mốc 4.200 và đỉnh 13/10 4.197). Ngược xu hướng chính – chỉ lướt, khối lượng nhỏ, hết sức thận trọng. Vào khi giá vào vùng bán và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng đỏ xác nhận, hoặc nến 1H đâm xuyên lên BB giữa rồi đóng lại dưới band; không dùng nến 15m/30m. Dừng lỗ 4.222 (trên BB90 trên 2H 4.214,6 và đỉnh tuần 4.217). TP1 4.185 – chốt 50–70%, dời SL hòa vốn; TP2 4.170. Nến 4H đóng trên 4.217 thì bỏ hẳn kế hoạch bán.
sellZones_en: Sell 4,203–4,212 (upper BB90: 45m 4,203.50 · 1H 4,208 · 3H/4H 4,209 · just above 4,200 and the Oct 13 high of 4,197). Counter-trend – scalp only, small size, extra caution. Enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it; never on a 15m/30m close. Stop 4,222 (above the 2H upper band at 4,214.60 and the 4,217 weekly high). TP1 4,185 – take 50–70%, stop to breakeven; TP2 4,170. A 4H close above 4,217 kills the short idea.
scenarios: Kết quả tin: 2 giờ qua không có tin đỏ; DXY trượt 101,73 rồi hồi 101,80, US10Y 5,073% → 5,102%; FedWatch ~87% Fed giữ lãi tháng 10 (CNBC).
Vì sao: USD yếu đẩy giá lên, lợi suất bật lại hãm đà; 45m–4H đều ở nửa trên BB90 nên nhịp chỉnh là cơ hội MUA.
Rủi ro: tối nay (thứ Sáu) không có tin đỏ Mỹ, Fed im lặng từ 17/10; chốt lời cuối tuần, tin Iran/Hormuz và cổ phiếu AI có thể làm giá giật mạnh – nến 4H/ngày đóng trên 4.200–4.217 mới mở đường 4.300.
scenarios_en: The data: no high-impact releases in the window; DXY slid to 101.73 then firmed to 101.80, the 10-year went 5.073% → 5.102%; FedWatch ~87% odds of an October hold (CNBC).
Why: a softer dollar lifted gold, a yield bounce capped it; with 45m–4H all in the upper half of BB90, dips are buys.

Risk: no high-impact U.S. data today and the Fed blackout starts Saturday; Friday profit-taking, Iran/Hormuz headlines and AI-stock jitters can whip price – only a 4H/daily close above 4,200–4,217 opens 4,300.

market_picture_en.text: Risk appetite is back: the STOXX 600 is up ~0.5% at 643.6 and on track for its best week since August (Reuters), S&P futures +0.2%, VIX 16.0. vn_gold_box.title: 💰 Vàng trong nước (vàng miếng SJC)
items: Giá vàng miếng SJC tại PNJ (cập nhật 14:48, kiểm tra lúc 15:48): mua 140,9 – bán 143,9 triệu đồng/lượng.
Biên độ trong ngày (các lần H79 ghi nhận): mua 140,3 – 140,9 triệu, bán 143,3 – 143,9 triệu. Chênh mua – bán 3,0 triệu đồng/lượng.

So với thế giới: 4.185,3 USD/oz (gold-api.com, 15:50) × 25.856 đồng/USD (tỷ giá thị trường open.er-api) × 1,20565 oz/lượng ≈ 130,5 triệu đồng/lượng → SJC bán ra cao hơn ≈ 13,4 triệu/lượng (sáng nay ≈ 13,9 triệu), chưa gồm thuế, phí.

Tin nước ngoài đang kéo vàng thế giới: (1) USD yếu, hướng tới tuần giảm đầu tiên sau 5 tuần (CNBC); (2) lợi suất 10 năm Mỹ quanh 5,1% sau PPI tháng 9 +6,3% so với cùng kỳ (CNBC); (3) Iran – Hormuz: Trump nói đang đàm phán nhưng vẫn dọa đánh thêm (Middle East Eye).

Lời khuyên vàng vật chất: vàng thế giới đang xác nhận nền 4.037–4.149, người cần mua vàng vật chất có thể mua lúc này, nên chia nhiều đợt vì chênh SJC – thế giới còn ~13,4 triệu và giá sắp tới sẽ biến động mạnh.

Why: softer yields and dollar, haven flows (AI stocks, Middle East), ETFs and central banks still buying; UBS and Goldman both target above $4,600.
Levels: base 4,037–4,149, near-term floor 4,147–4,160; a 4H/daily close above 4,200–4,217 opens 4,300–4,400.
Risk: FedWatch ~89% odds of a December hike, a yield rebound; below 4,147 means caution, below 4,037 invalidates the view.

market_picture_en.text: The 10-year Treasury yield dipped as low as 5.038%, a three-week low (WSJ), and the dollar is headed for its first weekly loss in five, with the DXY near 102.07 as AI stocks wobble (CNBC). Fed Chair Warsh offered no new signal, saying he doesn't prejudge meetings, while Middle East tensions keep a haven bid alive (FXStreet). The Street is still constructive: UBS sees $4,600 by December and calls dips toward $4,000 a chance to add; Goldman holds $4,650 for end-2026 and $5,400 for end-2027; global gold ETFs took in $10 billion in September to a record 4,256 metric tons, and China's central bank added 23 tons (World Gold Council). Counterpoints: FedWatch prices about 89% odds of a December hike, and several Indian funds halted bulk gold-ETF subscriptions (CNBC).

market_picture_en.text: Warsh offered no rate roadmap – only that the Fed will deliver price stability and decide at the October and December meetings – and the dollar slipped to 101.85 (FXStreet). Hot September PPI (1.3% m/m) didn't stop the 10-year from easing to about 5.07%, a 3-week low, with the DXY off its 18-month high (CNBC). The AI-stock selloff keeps a haven bid alive, and October hike odds sit near 29%. Gold's bounce is constructive, but the daily trend is still below its MA89 – a positive signal, not yet a long-term reversal.

Ông nhấn mạnh làn sóng đầu tư và AI tác động tới cầu trước cung (FXStreet). **Không có tín hiệu tăng lãi suất mới.**

Nến tuần trước (kết thúc 9/10) XANH: 4.142,3 → 4.193,8. Tuần này: mở 4.193,8, đáy 4.074,1 sau CPI/PPI nóng, nến ngày 15/10 đóng 4.170,2 (+1,6%), hiện ~4.183 – nến tuần đang có râu dưới dài, gần hòa giá mở.

sections.h: Đảo chiều dài hạn? Xác nhận hay phủ định
sections.p: Tích cực: giữ trên MA89 tuần (~3.987), bật mạnh từ 4.074, đã vượt trendline giảm từ 4.197. Chưa đủ: giá vẫn dưới MA89 ngày ~4.264 và giữa BB90 ngày ~4.261; trần 4.177–4.186 chưa phá. **Xác nhận:** đóng ngày trên 4.197 rồi trên ~4.265. **Phủ định:** đóng tuần dưới 4.074.

Lịch nhẹ: đơn trợ cấp thất nghiệp (19:30 22/10), PMI S&P Global sơ bộ (20:45 23/10), Michigan cuối (21:00 23/10). Fed im lặng từ 17/10 trước họp 27–28/10. Lịch ForexFactory tuần tới chưa phát hành – sẽ cập nhật.

At the IMF in Bangkok, Warsh said that since the September FOMC 'the world has broadly conformed to our expectations,' that the Fed 'would deliver price stability,' and that he doesn't 'believe in pre-judging meetings,' with judgments at the October and December meetings. He stressed the investment surge and said AI will hit demand before supply (FXStreet). **No fresh hike signal.**

Last week's candle (ended Oct 9) closed GREEN: 4,142.34 → 4,193.83. This week opened 4,193.83, hit 4,074.12 after hot CPI/PPI, closed Thursday at 4,170.25 (+1.6%) and trades near 4,183 – a long lower wick, roughly flat on the week.

sections.h: Long-term reversal? What confirms, what denies
sections.p: Positive: holding above the weekly MA89 (~3,987), a sharp bounce off 4,074 and a break of the down-trendline from 4,197. Not enough yet: price is below the daily MA89 (~4,264) and daily BB90 mid (~4,261), and 4,177–4,186 is unbroken. **Confirms:** a daily close above 4,197, then above ~4,265. **Denies:** a weekly close under 4,074.

Light slate: jobless claims (Thu 8:30 AM ET), S&P Global flash PMIs (Fri 9:45 AM ET), final UMich sentiment (Fri 10:00 AM ET). Fed blackout starts Oct 17 ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC. ForexFactory's next-week calendar isn't out yet.

sections.h: From the New York afternoon into the Asian open
sections.p: After the hot PPI print, gold flushed to 4,138, popped to 4,167, failed into the U.S. open and was back near 4,145 by 10:17 AM ET. Overnight, softer yields and a softer dollar powered a haven bid straight through prior resistance: Asian session low 4,145.50 at 1:00 PM ET → 4,159 at 3:00 PM ET → Asian high 4,176.90 at 4:00 PM ET (CNBC XAU= day high 4,176.94). From there it has ground lower: 6:00 PM ET 4,169 · 7:00 PM ET 4,163 · 7:50 PM ET 4,157.30 (gold-api.com ~4,158–4,159). December COMEX gold runs about $21.60 over spot.

The 4,177 spike landed right on the 4H BB90 mid/MA89 cluster (4,167 / 4,165) and the 78.6% Fib (4,171) of the 4,197→4,074 down-leg – higher-timeframe supply. The 4H and 3H are still in the lower half of their BB90 (mids 4,167 / 4,158), so the overnight rally was a pullback, not a trend flip. DXY holds near 102.04, the 10-year yield is around 5.08–5.09% (well off its post-CPI peak), Brent ~$105.70 and S&P futures ~7,777 – risk appetite stays cautious with the AI/data-center debt shakeout (CoreWeave CDS) still in play.

The H79 sell signal is already in from the high: price tagged the 4H mid/MA89 sell cluster and the 45m (5:45 / 6:30 / 7:15 PM ET) plus 1H (6:00 / 7:00 PM ET) candles closed red. If you're not in, sell a retrace into 4,165–4,175 (4H BB90 mid 4,167 · 4H MA89 4,165 · Fib 78.6% 4,171 · Asian high cluster 4,172–4,177) only on a red 45m or 1H close – never on a 15m/30m red close alone. Stop at 4,186 (above the 4,177 Asian high and R1 near 4,184). TP1 4,149 (45m mid/MA89), TP2 4,136 (50% Fib of the big down-leg · near the daily pivot at 4,131). A 1H close above 4,186 cancels the short. Buy only at 4,090–4,105 (lower BB90 on the 45m/4H/2H) on a 45m rejection wick with a bullish 45m MACD cross. Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 11:30 PM ET (high impact) – trim size ahead of it.

The 4H (BB90 mid 4,167) and 3H (4,158) sit in the lower half – primary trend down; the 45m/1H/2H briefly tagged the upper half on the overnight pop and are rotating back toward their mids. The 5m/15m/30m up-channel overnight was only a pullback and stalled at the 4H mid/MA89 cluster. MACD histogram: 5m −0.8 · 15m −1.8 · 30m −1.1 · 45m −0.4 (narrowing); 1H still +0.6. RSI(14) is oversold on the 5m (27) and mid-50s on the larger frames. Daily pivots from Oct 15 (H 4,167.10 · L 4,078.60 · C 4,147.60): P 4,131 · R1 4,184 · R2 4,220 · S1 4,095. Fib of the 4,197→4,074 drop: 50% 4,136 · 61.8% 4,150 · 78.6% 4,171 – the 4,177 Asian high sits on the 78.6%.

market_picture_en.text: Risk appetite is still weak: the AI selloff rolls on (Nasdaq −1.2% at the open), and the bid for Treasuries has the 10-year at 5.04–5.06%, around a three-week low. Since 10:00 AM ET, though, yields and the DXY (102.04) have firmed and Nasdaq futures have bounced, draining some of gold's haven bid. Brent is at $105.20 as the U.S. reportedly weighs renewed Iran strikes with the GBU-43. A 6.3% annual PPI keeps October hike odds near 34% – a longer-run headwind for gold.

sections.h: After the 8:30 AM ET data – PPI and retail sales (9:35 AM ET update; 3h filled ~11:37 AM ET)
sections.p: The numbers: September PPI rose 1.3% m/m (est. 0.6%, prior revised to 0.5%) and 6.3% y/y, the biggest annual gain since 2022; core PPI (ex food and energy) +0.7% (est. 0.3%); retail sales +0.8% (est. 0.3%) and ex-autos +0.9% (est. 0.6%). All four beat (BLS, Census via CNBC and Kitco). Spot path (CNBC XAU=, 5-minute bar opens): 3h before, 5:30 AM ET 4,158.60 · 1h before, 7:30 AM ET 4,155.70 · 30 min before, 8:00 AM ET 4,144.50 · release, 8:30 AM ET 4,149.80 · 30 min after, 9:00 AM ET 4,150.30 · 1h after, 9:30 AM ET 4,156.20 · 3h after, 11:30 AM ET 4,154.40 (+0.11%). The release bar flushed to 4,138.10 and snapped back; the post-data high was 4,167.10 at 9:15 AM ET, and spot was back at 4,151.60 by 9:34 AM ET (gold-api.com 4,154.70). Why it went the 'wrong' way: hot data should mean a firmer dollar, higher yields and weaker gold, and gold did drop $11 in the first five minutes. But traders looked under the hood. Energy drove most of the PPI jump as the Iran war keeps fuel prices high; PPI ex food, energy and trade rose just 0.5%, and retail sales ex autos and gas rose only 0.25% after roughly 1.1% in August, a sign consumers are pulling back. Meanwhile the tech selloff (Nasdaq futures −1.3%) pushed money into Treasuries: the 10-year yield fell 14 bps to 5.05% and the DXY slipped 0.5% to 102.07. Lower yields lifted gold even as October hike odds rose to about 34% (CME FedWatch via CNBC). Through the H79 lens: the pop stalled right at the 4H MA89/BB90 mid cluster (4,168–4,170), just under the 78.6% Fib at 4,171, which is the classic downtrend bounce failing at the higher-timeframe mid. Spot sits on the 45m mid (4,150) and below the 1H mid/MA89 (4,158). The 15m/30m channel is still up (price above the MA34/MA89), but both MACDs are below their signal lines and RSI is neutral at 52–58. The short isn't confirmed yet; it needs a red 45m or 1H close back below 4,150. The 8:15 AM ET plan was short 4,158–4,168 (stop 4,178) and long 4,092–4,102 (stop 4,080).

sections.h: Why gold is where it is
sections.p: The day's tailwinds are still in place: the DXY is at 102.13 (−0.4%), off its 18-month high; the 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.081% (−10.9 bps), around a three-week low; and Brent is at 104.75 (−1.2%). Fed officials Daly and Bowman have signaled no rush to hike at the Oct. 27–28 meeting. But risk appetite soured into the open: Nasdaq futures are down more than 1% on worries about AI companies' heavy borrowing, with S&P 500 futures off 0.3%, and the dollar ticked back up from 102.03 to 102.13. With PPI and retail sales minutes away, longs took profits into the 4,152–4,160 resistance cluster – the BB90 mid on the 45-minute, 2-hour, 3-hour and 1-hour charts.

sections.h: The 8:30 AM ET game plan (PPI + retail sales)
sections.p: Into the data (8:00–8:45 AM ET): no new positions. ForexFactory consensus: PPI +0.6% m/m (prior 0.4%), core PPI +0.3% (prior 0.2%), retail sales +0.3% (prior 1.2%), core retail sales +0.6% (prior 1.4%), alongside jobless claims (199K) and the Philly Fed (28.2). Scenario 1 – hot PPI / strong spending: the dollar and yields pop, gold likely breaks 4,136–4,140 (50% Fib · 30m mid/MA89) and heads to 4,114 (daily pivot), then the 4,092–4,102 buy zone. Scenario 2 – soft PPI / weak spending: gold bounces into 4,158–4,171, which is the high-probability H79 SELL area enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it. Only a 1H close above 4,171 (4H mid, 78.6% Fib) cancels the short and opens 4,197–4,202.

Per the H79 rule, the 45m (BB90 mid 4,152), 1H (4,159), 2H (4,154), 3H (4,159) and 4H (4,170) are all trading in the lower half of their bands – the primary trend is down and the 15m/5m bounce is just a pullback. sections.p: CPI Mỹ tháng 9 ra lúc 19:30 tăng 3,7% so với cùng kỳ, cao hơn dự báo 3,6%, chủ yếu do giá xăng. Vàng đang ở 4.153,7 (19:25) thì bị bán mạnh xuống 4.087 chỉ sau 15 phút, rồi trượt tiếp về 4.074,1 lúc 23:05 – thấp nhất kể từ 7/10. Phiên Mỹ đóng cửa 4.105,2 lúc 04:00, cả ngày 14/10 giảm khoảng 1,3%.

Mở cửa 05:00 ở 4.104, giá dò xuống đáy Á 4.099,9 lúc 06:05 rồi bật mạnh từ 07:10: chỉ trong 10 phút vàng vọt từ 4.116 lên 4.142, đúng lúc bài phỏng vấn của bà Daly (Fed San Francisco) được đăng – Fed có thể còn phải tăng lãi nhưng không cần vội ở tháng 10. Nhịp thứ hai 09:45–10:00 đưa giá lên đỉnh Á 4.161,1 lúc 10:00, cùng lúc DXY chạm đáy 101,88. Sau đỉnh, lực chốt lời kéo giá về 4.131,9 lúc 13:00; phiên Á đóng 4.135,7 – vẫn tăng khoảng 32 giá so với mở cửa.

Mở 14:00 ở 4.136, giá đi lên đều: vượt 4.150 lúc 15:00–15:15 và lên đỉnh 4.160,2 lúc 16:35 – thấp hơn đỉnh Á đúng 1 giá. Cả hai lần chạm 4.160–4.161 đều bị bán xuống. Lúc 17:50 giá quanh 4.154 (gold-api.com 4.155,5–4.156 lúc 17:59–18:00), tăng khoảng 49 giá (+1,2%) so với giá chốt hôm qua 4.105. Như vậy vàng đã lấy lại toàn bộ cú rơi sau CPI.

Thứ nhất, USD hạ nhiệt: DXY từ 102,53 đầu phiên Á xuống 102,06 (−0,5%), rời đỉnh 18 tháng lập hôm qua. Thứ hai, lợi suất 10 năm Mỹ còn 5,085% (−10,5 điểm cơ bản), thấp nhất 3 tuần, 2 năm 4,74% – tiền trú ẩn chảy vào trái phiếu khi cổ phiếu công nghệ châu Á bị bán tháo. Thứ ba, Fed bớt diều hâu: Daly nói chưa cần tăng lãi ở cuộc họp 27–28/10, Bowman muốn chờ thêm; FedWatch còn khoảng 29% khả năng tăng lãi tháng 10, từ mức 50% ngay sau CPI. Thứ tư, dầu giảm: Brent từ 106 về 104,6 (đáy 103,4 lúc 15:20) khi Mỹ tính nới trừng phạt nhóm tàu chở dầu bị cấm vận, dù eo Hormuz vẫn nóng – tàu GFS Pride của Singapore bị đánh chìm, Iran dọa tấn công tàu chiến Mỹ. Dầu hạ bớt lo lạm phát. Dù vậy, Ole Hansen (Saxo) vẫn cho rằng bức tranh kỹ thuật của vàng còn mong manh.

19:30: PPI tháng 9 (dự báo +0,6% m/m, kỳ trước 0,4%), PPI lõi (+0,3%, trước 0,2%), doanh số bán lẻ (+0,3%, trước 1,2%) và bán lẻ lõi (+0,6%, trước 1,4%) – cả bốn đều là tin đỏ trên ForexFactory; cùng giờ có đơn trợ cấp thất nghiệp (dự báo 199K) và chỉ số Philly Fed (28,2). PPI nóng cộng bán lẻ mạnh sẽ kéo USD và lợi suất bật lại, vàng dễ mất nhịp hồi; PPI mềm có thể giúp vàng thử lại vùng 4.160–4.171. 10:30 sáng mai (16/10) Chủ tịch Fed Warsh phát biểu tại hội nghị IMF – World Bank, cũng là tin đỏ.

Giá 4.154 vừa nhích lên trên BB90 giữa 45m (4.151) và MA89 (4.151), MA34 còn thấp ở 4.122; dải trên 4.211, dải dưới 4.091. MACD 45m dương nhưng histogram thu hẹp dần (+7,9 lúc 10:45 xuống +2,4), RSI14 61 – lực hồi đang yếu đi. Bộ lọc H79: 15m kênh tăng (giá > MA34 4.147 > MA89 4.121), 5m dẹt quanh MA34 4.155, 30m chưa thành kênh tăng (MA34 4.130 còn dưới MA89 4.141) → đây là nhịp hồi trong xu hướng giảm, dễ dừng ở cụm BB giữa/MA89 khung lớn 4.159–4.171. Pivot ngày: P 4.114 · R1 4.154 · R2 4.202 · S1 4.065. Fib sóng giảm 4.197 (13/10) → 4.074: 50% 4.136, 61,8% 4.150 (đã vượt), 78,6% 4.171 – trùng BB giữa 4H. Tín hiệu BÁN đẹp: giá vào 4.160–4.170 — vào khi giá vào vùng bán và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng đỏ xác nhận, hoặc nến 1H đâm xuyên lên BB giữa rồi đóng lại dưới band (dưới 4.160), chắc hơn khi 45m đóng dưới BB giữa 4.151.

sections.p: September CPI landed at 8:30 AM ET Wednesday at 3.7% y/y, above the 3.6% consensus, driven mostly by gasoline. Gold was at 4,153.70 at 8:25 AM ET and got hit down to 4,087 within 15 minutes, then slid to 4,074.10 at 12:05 PM ET – its lowest since Oct. 7. It settled at 4,105.20 at 5:00 PM ET, down about 1.3% on the day.

Gold opened at 4,104 at 6:00 PM ET and dipped to the Asian low of 4,099.90 at 7:05 PM ET before ripping higher from 8:10 PM ET: in ten minutes it ran from 4,116 to 4,142 as San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly's interview hit the wires – more hikes are likely, but there's no rush in October. A second leg at 10:45–11:00 PM ET carried it to the Asian high of 4,161.10 at 11:00 PM ET, right as the DXY bottomed at 101.88. Profit-taking pulled it back to 4,131.90 by 2:00 AM ET, and Asia closed at 4,135.70 – still up about $32 from the open.

London opened at 4,136 at 3:00 AM ET and gold climbed steadily, clearing 4,150 at 4:00–4:15 AM ET and peaking at 4,160.20 at 5:35 AM ET – exactly a dollar shy of the Asian high. Both runs at 4,160–4,161 were sold. At 6:50 AM ET gold was hovering near 4,154 (gold-api.com 4,155.50–4,156 at 6:59–7:00 AM ET), up about $49 (+1.2%) from yesterday's 4,105 settle. In other words, the entire post-CPI drop has been erased.

First, the dollar cooled: the DXY slipped from 102.53 at the Asian open to 102.06 (−0.5%), backing off Wednesday's 18-month high. Second, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 5.085% (−10.5 bps), a three-week low, with the 2-year at 4.74% – haven money rotated into bonds as Asian tech stocks sold off. Third, the Fed sounded less hawkish: Daly sees no need to hike at the Oct. 27–28 meeting and Bowman wants to wait; FedWatch now shows about 29% odds of an October hike, down from 50% right after CPI. Fourth, oil eased: Brent dropped from 106 to 104.60 (low of 103.40 at 4:20 AM ET) as Washington weighs easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet' tankers, even though Hormuz remains hot – Singapore's GFS Pride was sunk and Iran threatened U.S. warships. Cheaper oil takes some heat off inflation fears. Still, Saxo's Ole Hansen calls gold's technical outlook fragile.

8:30 AM ET: September PPI (est. +0.6% m/m, prior 0.4%), core PPI (+0.3%, prior 0.2%), retail sales (+0.3%, prior 1.2%) and core retail sales (+0.6%, prior 1.4%) – all four high-impact on ForexFactory – plus initial jobless claims (est. 199K) and the Philly Fed index (est. 28.2). A hot PPI with strong spending would lift the dollar and yields and likely cap the bounce; a soft print could send gold back to test 4,160–4,171. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at 11:30 PM ET at the IMF–World Bank meetings, another high-impact event.

At 4,154, gold has just edged above the 45m BB90 mid (4,151) and MA89 (4,151), with MA34 well below at 4,122; upper band 4,211, lower band 4,091. sections.p: Từ 13:45 vàng giao ngay ~4.136 đi lên đều, vượt 4.150 khoảng 15:00 và chạm đỉnh ~4.160 lúc 15:25 – đúng mép dưới vùng bán 4.155–4.168. Sau đó giá bị đẩy về ~4.151–4.153 lúc 15:55. Hai giờ đầu phiên Âu vàng tăng ~16 giá.

USD và lợi suất Mỹ tiếp tục lùi: DXY ~102,06 (−0,5%), lợi suất 10 năm ~5,09% (−10 điểm cơ bản) theo CNBC. Brent giảm ~2% về ~103,8 USD dù Hormuz vẫn nóng (tàu Singapore bị đánh chìm, Iran dọa tàu chiến Mỹ), vì Mỹ tính nới trừng phạt tàu chở dầu. Chứng khoán châu Âu mở cửa giảm theo đợt bán công nghệ ở châu Á – tiền chạy vào trái phiếu.

Lợi suất và USD giảm làm vàng hấp dẫn hơn. Các quan chức Fed Daly và Bowman nói chưa cần tăng lãi ngay tháng 10, nên cược tăng lãi hạ xuống (FedWatch ~27% theo CNBC/Reuters). Dầu giảm cũng bớt lo lạm phát. Lực mua đủ đẩy giá hồi, nhưng chưa đủ phá cụm BB giữa.

Đúng kịch bản: chờ hồi lên BB giữa để bán. Giá hồi lên ~4.160 và chững ngay dưới cụm BB giữa 45m/2H (~4.155), trùng Fib 50–61,8% sóng giảm 4.224 → 4.073 (~4.149–4.166). Lệnh bán khớp mép dưới vùng, chưa tới TP1 4.140, SL 4.178 chưa chạm. Vùng mua 4.097–4.110 không khớp.

45m–4H vẫn dưới BB giữa nên xu hướng chính là giảm; 15m kênh tăng chỉ là nhịp hồi. Nến 45m 14:30 đóng sát trên BB giữa, nến 15:15 đang đỏ quay lại dưới – nếu nến đóng 16:00 giữ dưới ~4.155 là tín hiệu bán H79 rõ hơn. MACD 45m vẫn dương nên vào khối lượng nhỏ. Trước tin dễ giằng co 4.140–4.165.

19:30 PPI (dự báo 0,6% m/m, lõi 0,3%) và bán lẻ (0,3%). Không vào lệnh mới 19:00–19:45. PPI nóng → USD, lợi suất bật → vàng dễ quay về 4.140 rồi 4.125, sâu hơn là vùng mua 4.097–4.110. PPI mềm → vàng có thể thử 4.168–4.178; nến 1H đóng trên 4.175 thì bỏ lệnh bán. Sau tin chỉ bán khi giá vào vùng bán và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng đỏ xác nhận, hoặc nến 1H đâm xuyên lên BB giữa rồi đóng lại dưới band; nếu đóng trên thì đứng ngoài phiên.

sections.p: From 2:45 AM ET, spot gold climbed steadily from ~4,136, cleared 4,150 around 4:00 AM ET and hit ~4,160 at 4:25 AM ET – right at the bottom of the 4,155–4,168 sell zone. It then slipped back to ~4,151–4,153 by 4:55 AM ET, about +16 points over the first two hours of London.

The dollar and Treasury yields kept easing: DXY ~102.06 (−0.5%), U.S. 10-year ~5.09% (−10 bps), per CNBC. Brent fell ~2% to ~$103.8 even as Hormuz stays tense (a Singapore ship sunk, Iran threatening U.S. warships), as Washington weighs easing tanker sanctions. European stocks opened lower after Asia's tech selloff, sending money into bonds.

Lower yields and a softer dollar made bullion more attractive. Fed officials Daly and Bowman signaled no rush to hike in October, trimming hike bets (FedWatch ~27%, per CNBC/Reuters). Cheaper oil also eased inflation worries. Buyers lifted gold into the bounce but couldn't clear the mid-band cluster.

On script: the plan was to sell a bounce into the mid-band. Gold rallied to ~4,160 and stalled just under the 45m/2H BB mid (~4,155), overlapping the 50–61.8% retracement of the 4,224 → 4,073 drop (~4,149–4,166). Shorts filled at the bottom of the zone; TP1 4,140 not hit yet, stop 4,178 untouched. The 4,097–4,110 buy zone did not fill.

45m through 4H remain below the BB mid, so the primary trend is down; the 15m up-channel is just a pullback. The 3:30 AM ET 45m candle closed right above the mid-band, and the 4:15 AM ET candle is red back below it – a close under ~4,155 at 5:00 AM ET would firm up the H79 sell signal. The 45m MACD is still positive, so keep size small. Expect chop between 4,140 and 4,165 into the data.

PPI (est. +0.6% m/m, core +0.3%) and retail sales (est. +0.3%) at 8:30 AM ET. No new trades 8:00–8:45 AM ET. A hot PPI lifts the dollar and yields → gold likely back to 4,140, then 4,125, with the 4,097–4,110 buy zone below. A soft print could test 4,168–4,178; a 1-hour close above 4,175 cancels the short. After the release, sell only — enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it; a close above it means sit the session out.

sections.p: Tuesday's US session sold gold off from 4,193 (8:30 AM ET) to 4,148 (1:50 PM ET), settling near 4,162 – a second straight down day, roughly 0.8% lower over two sessions.

Gold opened at 4,163 at 6:00 PM ET and slipped to the Asian low of 4,145 at 9:45 PM ET before bouncing to the Asian high of 4,172 at 11:15 PM ET – about five hours after the open – on dovish comments from the NY Fed's Williams. Sellers then picked the prior move back up, and Asia closed at 4,149.
High of 4,159 at 4:15 AM ET, low of 4,141 at 6:25 AM ET – the low of the day. Heading into 7:00 AM ET, gold was hovering around 4,138–4,144.

A slightly softer dollar (DXY ~102.1) and long-end Treasury yields down 3–4 bps kept the slide contained. But Brent above $106 on renewed Middle East attacks revived inflation worries. Williams sees one more hike this year but none in 2027, while Waller and Goolsbee leaned hawkish on AI-driven price pressure. Markets price roughly 90% odds of a December hike – higher rates remain the main headwind for gold.
September CPI at 8:30 AM ET: headline est. 3.6% y/y; core est. +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. A hot print would lift the dollar and yields and pressure gold; a soft one would support a bounce.

Price is below MA34 (4,162) and MA89 (4,176), hugging the lower BB90 (2 SD) at 4,142 (mid 4,176, upper 4,211). Daily pivots: P 4,171 · R1 4,194 · S1 4,139 · S2 4,116. Into the NY open, expect chop between 4,139 and 4,163 until CPI: a hot core print could break S1 toward 4,116; a soft one could lift price back to 4,162–4,171.

strategies.title_en: Asian session, Oct 13: gold ranges below 4,205, downtrend still in control – all eyes on Wednesday’s CPI
strategies.trend_en: Bearish (daily below the 20/50 EMA; H4 below its 20/50 EMA, ranging tightly 4,183–4,202 since Monday's New York session)
entryZones_en: Probe long: 4,168–4,178 (Oct 12 low 4,178.1 · pivot S1 4,168.6 · Oct 1 low 4,169.4), stop below 4,148 (under the Oct 5 low 4,150.4)
Stronger long: 4,128–4,141 (pivot S2 4,141.2 · Oct 6 low 4,130.7 · Oct 8 low 4,128.1), stop below 4,088 (under pivot S3 4,104.4 and the Oct 7 swing low 4,091.2)
sellZones_en: Sell the rally (preferred): 4,197–4,206 (H4 50 EMA 4,196.6 · Asian-session high 4,201.7 · pivot P 4,205.4 · high of the 4:00 AM ET H4 bar Oct 12 4,205.7), stop above 4,230 (high of the 12:00 AM ET H4 bar Oct 12 4,228.5)
Stronger short: 4,233–4,243 (pivot R1 4,232.8 · Oct 9 high 4,233.7 · Oct 12 high 4,242.3, near the daily 20 EMA 4,249), stop above 4,262 (above the Oct 2 swing high 4,259.0)
H4 close above 4,230 → drop the rally short, wait for 4,233–4,243; a daily close above 4,260 → bearish scenario off
scenarios_en: The data: no tier-1 Tue Oct 13; gold ranging below 4,205; daily/H4 under the 20/50 EMAs – downtrend (CNBC).
The tape: Asian range 4,183–4,202; DXY 102.57 near an 18-month high; 10-year ~5.24% near highs since 2002.
Why: strong dollar and high yields weigh on gold; FedWatch ~81% chance of a hold in October (CNBC/Kitco).
Levels: sell rallies under 4,205 → 4,178 then 4,169; buy 4,168–4,178; break of 4,169 → 4,141.
Risk: thin Asian liquidity; CPI Wed 8:30 AM ET (est. 3.6% y/y) – wait for an M15 close to confirm.
strategies.physicalAdvice_en: Trade the plan, not the noise.
macro_en: CNBC (Reuters, Oct 12): the dollar index rose 0.3% to 102.57, just under an 18-month high; CME FedWatch shows 81% odds of an October hold. Kitco: gold closed Monday down 0.6% around $4,169.
CNBC: the 10-year Treasury yield around 5.24% – near its highest since 2002 (bond market closed for Columbus Day Oct 12); high rates keep weighing on gold.
CNBC (Oct 12): Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack says a restrictive stance is appropriate and favors hiking in 'small but relatively quick steps'.
CNBC/AFP: Ukraine says Russia broke the 'energy ceasefire'; Iran hit another tanker in Hormuz; Brent settled at $106.65 (+1.8%) – the 'oil → inflation → rates' channel is bearish for gold.
Reuters: China's central bank bought gold for a 23rd straight month (about 23 tonnes in September) – long-term support at lower prices.
strategies.notes_en: Technicals use COMEX gold futures (GC=F, Yahoo Finance); spot XAU/USD trades about $18 lower (gold-api.com: 4,168.8 at 8:22 PM ET Oct 12) – for XAU/USD orders subtract about $18 from the levels above.

strategies.title: Vàng mất mốc 4.200, thủng EMA H4 – xu hướng giảm, chờ CPI tối thứ Tư
strategies.trend: Giảm (D1 dưới EMA20/EMA50, H4 vừa xuống dưới EMA20/EMA50)
entryZones: Mua thăm dò: 4.170 – 4.178 USD/oz (đáy phiên 12/10 4.178,1 · pivot S1 4.170,4 · đáy 01/10 4.169,4), dừng lỗ dưới 4.148 (dưới đáy 05/10 4.150,4)
sellZones: Bán mạnh: 4.242 – 4.259 USD/oz (đỉnh 12/10 4.242,3 · pivot R1 4.248,0 · đỉnh swing 02/10 4.259,0), dừng lỗ trên 4.285 (trên pivot R2 4.279,6)
Nếu nến H4 đóng trên 4.230 → bỏ lệnh bán hồi, chờ vùng 4.242 – 4.259; đóng cửa ngày trên 4.260 → bỏ kịch bản giảm
scenarios: Bối cảnh: vàng mất 4.200, thủng EMA H4; D1/H4 dưới EMA – xu hướng giảm, chờ CPI thứ Tư (FXStreet/CNBC).
Diễn biến: đầu Á từng 4.206 rồi hạ; FXStreet XAU/USD ~−1,5% về 4.163; WTI >93 USD (Hormuz/Houthi).
Vì sao: kênh dầu → lạm phát → lãi suất; USD và rủi ro địa chính trị đè vàng sau nhịp bật 'ngừng bắn năng lượng'.
Rủi ro: CPI 19:30 14/10 (dự báo 3,6% y/y); nóng → dễ thủng 4.170; mềm → có thể bật 4.242–4.259.
strategies.physicalAdvice: Làm theo kế hoạch, đừng chạy theo nến tin.
macro: CNBC/Reuters (12/10): đầu phiên Á vàng giao ngay lên 4.206 USD/oz, cao nhất từ 02/10, nhờ dầu và USD yếu sau tuyên bố 'ngừng bắn năng lượng' Nga – Ukraine; sau đó hạ nhiệt khi thị trường chờ CPI thứ Tư.

FXStreet (02:08 13/10 giờ VN): XAU/USD giảm khoảng 1,5% về 4.163 USD; dầu WTI vượt 93 USD do Houthi tấn công Ả Rập Xê Út và Iran tấn công tàu ở eo Hormuz – kênh 'dầu → lạm phát → lãi suất' bất lợi cho vàng.
DXY tăng 0,3% lên 102,56; lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ 10 năm 5,242% – mặt bằng lãi suất cao tiếp tục đè giá vàng (FXStreet).
Thị trường định giá ~20% khả năng Fed tăng 0,25 điểm % ở cuộc họp 27–28/10 và gần 90% cho tháng 12 (FXStreet dẫn Prime Terminal). Lãi suất hiện tại 3,75–4,00% (Fed, 16/09).

strategies.trend_en: Bearish (daily below the 20/50 EMA, H4 just slipped below its 20/50 EMA)
entryZones_en: Probe long: 4,170–4,178 (Oct 12 low 4,178.1 · pivot S1 4,170.4 · Oct 1 low 4,169.4), stop below 4,148 (under the Oct 5 low 4,150.4)
Stronger long: 4,124–4,131 (Oct 6 low 4,130.7 · Oct 8 low 4,128.1 · pivot S2 4,124.4), stop below 4,085 (Oct 7 swing low 4,091.2 · pivot S3 4,092.8)
sellZones_en: Sell the rally (preferred): 4,197–4,205 (H4 50 EMA 4,196.9 · pivot P 4,202.0 · high of the 4:00 AM ET H4 bar Oct 12 4,205.7), stop above 4,230 (high of the 12:00 AM ET H4 bar Oct 12 4,228.5)
Stronger short: 4,242–4,259 (Oct 12 high 4,242.3 · pivot R1 4,248.0 · Oct 2 swing high 4,259.0), stop above 4,285 (above pivot R2 4,279.6)
H4 close above 4,230 → drop the rally short, wait for 4,242–4,259; a daily close above 4,260 → bearish scenario off
scenarios_en: The data: gold lost 4,200 and broke the H4 EMA; daily/H4 under the EMAs – downtrend into Wednesday CPI (FXStreet/CNBC).
The tape: Asian open tagged 4,206 then faded; FXStreet XAU/USD ~−1.5% to 4,163; WTI >$93 (Hormuz/Houthi).
Why: oil → inflation → rates channel; dollar and geopolitics capped the bounce after the 'energy ceasefire' pop.
Levels: sell rallies under 4,202 → 4,178 then 4,170; buy 4,170–4,178; break of 4,170 → 4,128–4,091.
Risk: CPI Wed 8:30 AM ET (est. 3.6% y/y); hot → break 4,170; soft → pop toward 4,242–4,259.
strategies.physicalAdvice_en: Trade the plan, not the noise.
macro_en: CNBC/Reuters (Oct 12): early in Asia spot gold rose to $4,206/oz, its highest since Oct 2, on softer oil and the dollar after the Russia–Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' announcement; it then cooled as the market waits on Wednesday's CPI.

FXStreet (3:08 PM ET Oct 12): XAU/USD down about 1.5% at $4,163; WTI above $93 after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iran hitting ships in Hormuz – the 'oil → inflation → rates' channel is bearish for gold.
DXY up 0.3% at 102.56; the 10-year Treasury yield 5.242% – high rates keep weighing on gold (FXStreet).
Markets price ~20% odds of a 25 bp Fed hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting and nearly 90% by December (FXStreet citing Prime Terminal). Current range 3.75–4.00% (Fed, Sep 16).
